## Example 5.1 · Parts (a–b) {#iv5-example-5-1-ab .vector-lesson .magnitude-lesson .geometric-lesson }


Consider the diagram below, where $\overrightarrow{OA}$ and $\overrightarrow{OB}$ are position vectors to the points $A(a_x,a_y)$ and $B(b_x,b_y)$ respectively.

<div class="m-split g-proof-layout">
<div><img class="g-booklet-triangle" src="../media/example-5-1.svg" alt="Original booklet diagram: position vectors a from O to A and b from O to B, with theta between them and side AB joining their heads."></div>
<div>
<p><strong>a)</strong> Express <span data-math="\overrightarrow{AB}"></span> in terms of <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}"></span> and <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{b}"></span></p>
<p><strong>b)</strong> Calculate <span data-math="|\overrightarrow{OA}|"></span>, <span data-math="|\overrightarrow{OB}|"></span> and <span data-math="|\overrightarrow{AB}|"></span></p>
<div data-module="reveal-panel" class="m-reveal"><button class="toggle-panel" aria-pressed="false">Show check</button><div class="panel-answer" hidden><div class="m-equation"><span data-math="\overrightarrow{AB}=\underset{\sim}{b}-\underset{\sim}{a}"></span></div><div class="m-equation"><span data-math="|\overrightarrow{OA}|=\sqrt{a_x^2+a_y^2}"></span></div><div class="m-equation"><span data-math="|\overrightarrow{OB}|=\sqrt{b_x^2+b_y^2}"></span></div><div class="m-equation"><span data-math="|\overrightarrow{AB}|=\sqrt{(b_x-a_x)^2+(b_y-a_y)^2}"></span></div></div></div></div></div>
<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet Example 5.1(a–b) · p. 36</div>

::: notes
Keep the original diagram visible while students work. The direction A→B gives b−a. Magnitudes are non-negative scalars. For part (c), square the distance expression before expanding; avoid needless manipulation of square roots. The diagram is cropped directly from the supplied booklet with text converted to SVG paths.
:::
